{"additions":348,"author":{"id":"U_kgDOD0kEpA","is_bot":false,"login":"evisdren","name":""},"baseRefName":"main","body":"## Why

`groupReposByCell` fans out to **every** placement of a repo — home and mirrors alike. Its comment claims this matches the BFF; the BFF does the opposite (`canonicalPlacement` in entire.io `list-repos-index.ts`: the placement whose id equals the row id, else the first). Mirror namespaces are replicated copies of the same content, so the extra legs return duplicate and stale rows, and CLI results diverge from the web.

Measured on `entirehq/peregrine` (3 ready placements: us-east-2 canonical, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-2), query `repo id remap`:

- web / leaf canonical namespace: **6 rows**
- CLI: **100 rows** — provably the union of all three namespaces; 94 rows came from mirror namespaces (mostly ap-southeast-2, whose query-serve currently admits rows down to rerank 0.22 where us-east-2 floors at ~0.45 — that config skew is a separate issue)
- EU namespace is a strict subset of US (replica + index lag): mirrors hold no unique content

## What

- `groupReposByCell` routes each entry to its **canonical placement only**: ID match against the entry's ID, else `placements[0]` — the BFF's exact rule, so web and CLI search the same namespace for the same repo. Selection never keys on the `Mirror` flag (real `/repos` rows mark every placement `Mirror:true`, canonical included).
- A canonical placement that is explicitly not ready (`processing`/`failed`/`suspended`) is skipped and reported; semantic search surfaces it as a warning instead of silently narrowing scope. Empty status (older cores) stays routable.
- Code search gets the same canonical-only grouping (its mirror-dedupe merge logic remains as a safety net).

## Why

entire-core `/repos` now exposes `primaries.processing` — the placement in the cell that does the repo's heavy lifting (trails, runners, checkpoint ingest), which is where searchable content originates. The CLI now routes search by that election (entireio/cli#2044); the web must apply the same rule or the two clients diverge the moment core elects a processing primary that differs from the row-ID convention — the exact failure mode ENT-1672 exists to kill.

## What

- New `searchPlacement(row)` in `list-repos-index.ts`: the placement named by `primaries.processing` when it resolves, else the `canonicalPlacement` convention (rows predating the field). Unlike `processingPlacement` (editor-DO routing), an elected-but-unready primary is returned as-is instead of silently falling back to a different cell — a fallback would search a placement core says is not the processing home, and the CLI skips-with-report on the same pick; the two clients must choose identically.
- **Semantic search, filtered:** routes by `searchPlacement` and pins the **placement's** ULID upstream instead of the row id (query-serve resolves any accessible placement id for explicit filters). **Semantic search, broad:** stays on the canonical convention — query-serve narrows a pin-less search to the placements canonical (row id) in its own cell, so routing a divergently elected repo's broad query to the elected cell would search it nowhere. Unify once the leaves narrow broad scope by the election.
- **Code search: canonical in both modes, deliberately.** Code content is placement-replicated git data (nothing code-searchable originates only in the elected cell, unlike processing-derived semantic docs), and every follow-up read from a hit (`/symbols`, `/usages`, the file viewer) resolves the canonical placement — canonical is the one read set that keeps a hit and its follow-ups on the same copy.
- Not-ready placements are skipped explicitly (review findings): a filtered semantic search whose scope narrowed rides `partial` + `coverage_incomplete`; all-skipped answers 200 with empty results (never a client 404 for an index-resolved repo); code search counts the skip in `unrouted`. `accessible_repos` requires BOTH the search and canonical placements ready (with split routing, either gate alone advertises a repo one request shape never searches) and keys the post-gate mask by the **canonical** cell — the only cell whose advertisement is authoritative for a row id — so a divergent election can't drop valid repos.
- `accessible_repos` still advertises the row id (caller-facing repo identity and slug-resolution round-trip are unchanged).

## Validation

- New `searchPlacement` unit tests: election preferred over convention, fallback on absent/unresolvable election, elected-but-unready returned as-is.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; search (98), list-repos-index (incl. 6 new), and code-search suites pass; oxfmt clean.
- Behavior is identical today for every repo where the election matches the convention (all current rows); the change pins the rule for when they diverge.

## Notes

- entire-search's own broad-scope narrowing (`core_repos_resolver.go`) and its `accessible_repos` advertisement still use the row-ID convention leaf-side; that needs the same processing-primary preference before core elects a primary that differs — tracked under ENT-1672.
